summary.text: A female neonate born at 39 weeks of gestation by spontaneous vaginal delivery to a 32 year-old mother (birth weight 3650 g, Apgar 7/8) was admitted to the NICU on the day of birth with suspected congenital heart disease. She had labored breathing, tachypnoea and signs of volume overload, with an enlarged, severely oedematous, hyperaemic left upper extremity and shoulder bearing a geographic port-wine stain, hyperthermia, thrills and a mild systolic murmur.

Echocardiography showed right-sided volume overload and raised suspicion of an aortic arch anomaly and arteriovenous malformation; X-ray showed cardiomegaly and left upper extremity bone changes. Milrinone, furosemide and spironolactone were started. On the second day of life CT angiography showed a dilated left subclavian artery, an arteriovenous fistula to the left brachiocephalic vein and an arteriovenous malformation of the left scapula and shoulder. Sequencing at two months found a pathogenic heterozygous RASA1 variant, and Parkes Weber syndrome was genetically confirmed.

Milrinone was stopped on the fifth day and diuretics were weaned and stopped; the therapy was discontinued before discharge. The patient moved to the neonatal ward after 9 days and was discharged at 25 days without signs of cardiovascular insufficiency. Four embolizations followed at 5 weeks, 5 months, 10 months and 16 months, using coils and Histoacryl glue; the murmur and thrill disappeared after the second. During the fourth procedure angiography still showed a dilated left subclavian artery and multiple fistulas to the left cephalic vein; one was closed with Histoacryl glue and two with coils, and the patent ductus arteriosus was closed with an Amplatzer Duct Occluder II.

At 16 months the left arm was less edematous and hyperaemic, with hyperemia and the port-wine stain visible when crying or supine; the left upper arm diameter was 21 cm against 16 cm on the right. She wears a compression garment, sees a physiotherapist, has no signs of heart failure and takes no medications. One parent carries the same variant and is asymptomatic, with a head MRI planned.
